name: Auxiliares Marcomanni seniores (palatina)

abilities.name: Barbarian Testudo
abilities.text: The troops of this unit raise their shields above their heads in a static defensive formation.

abilities.name: Spear Wall
abilities.text: The unit moves into close wall formation.

abilities.name: Square
abilities.text: The unit moves into a close square formation. Note that it cannot move whilst this ability is active.

attributes.name: Snipe
attributes.text: This unit remains hidden while firing.

attributes.name: Guerrilla Deployment
attributes.text: This unit can deploy outside of the deployment zone.

attributes.name: Hide (scrub & forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in scrub and forest until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Immune to Fear
attributes.text: This unit is immune to the fear effects of scary units.

attributes.name: Impetuous
attributes.text: This unit gets an extra morale bonus when eager.

attributes.name: Disciplined
attributes.text: This unit does not suffer a morale penalty when the general dies. It can also rally after routing more often.

short: The name Marcomanni is tribal and belongs to a group of ancient Germanic tribes belonging to the Suebi. Marcomanni (Latin Marcoman(n)i, German Marcomannen –«inhabitants of the frontiers») left Thuringia and Saxony under the pressure of the Cimbri and Teutons around 100 BC and migrated to the area on the upper and middle Main. In the 70s BC they took part in the Celtic wars on the side of the Arverni and Sequani against the Aedui. In 58 BC the Marcomanni fought in alliance with other Germanic tribes under Ariovistus against Caesar. After the expedition of Drusus the Elder, they moved to Bohemia (around 8 BC). There they formed a tribal alliance that included the Quadi, Langobards, Semnones and Hermunduri; this union Augustus considered a potential danger to Rome and intended to destroy it, but these plans were hindered by a rebellion in Pannonia. In the late 4th century Christianity spread among the Marcomanni. In 433 they were subjected to the Huns and participated in Attila's campaign in Gaul (451). At the end of the 5th century, they left Bohemia and migrated to Bavaria, where they joined the Bavarian tribal union.
history: In the face of an increasing number of barbarian incursions, the effective defence of Rome’s now-sprawling territory became a serious problem in the 4th century AD. The Emperor Constantine’s controversial solution was to divide the army into two halves. 'Limitanei', literally ‘the men on the limes’ or 'borders', were frontier garrison troops intended to pin down an invading force until the full-time 'comitatenses', the late-Roman equivalent of the traditional Legionaries, could arrive to deal with the situation decisively. Although well-equipped, limitanei were generally considered by all to be second-class warriors. This was possibly because they were often part-time soldiers who had been encouraged to settle and farm the land around their outposts in exchange for policing the Empire's borders.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
